idiom_name: opaque struct + const-correct accessor functions (no mutators)
implementation_notes: C has no immutability declaration, so the pattern is a module discipline: define the struct only in the implementation file (leave the header with an incomplete type), hand instances out and take them in through functions that accept const pointers, and provide no mutator - a logical update returns a newly allocated value. const is the only relevant primitive and it is shallow and not transitive, so a caller that keeps a non-const pointer can still write to the same object; the const-correct API is a contract rather than a guarantee. Hiding the layout, and copying strings and arrays into and out of the module, is what turns that contract into an enforceable boundary.
pitfalls: const is not transitive in C: a pointer to a const struct still yields non-const members, so an accessor that returns int * from a const object hands out write access.
Declaring the struct body in the public header lets any caller write its fields directly; only an incomplete type plus accessor functions keeps the state private.
Deep constness must be threaded through every aggregate type, and a const object still needs an ownership rule for values derived from it (who frees the returned Money?).
The compiler cannot see through casts: an API that exposes void * or a non-const back-door defeats const correctness without a diagnostic.
